newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pernod studies share buyback plan.
newsitem.headline: Pernod studies share buyback plan.

text.p: French drinks group Pernod-Ricard is studying the possibility of buying back shares on the market after having received the authorisation to do so at its annual general meeting in May, a spokesman said.
"Obviously the lower the price, the more attractive the prospect of buying back one's own shares, but we're not doing that right now," the spokesman told Reuters. "It's a possibility we're studying."
The stock, which fell sharply last week on disappointing first-half results, was 1.15 percent higher at 281.50 francs at 0850 GMT on the Paris bourse.
The stock closed last Friday at 278.30 francs, just above its year low of 277 francs.
Pernod last week reported net attributable profit rose to 504 million francs from 490 million, but operating profit slipped to 771 million from 790 million.
The stock has also been under pressure from planned increases in alcohol tax announced in the 1997 budget.
